correctness.rationale: Connectedness gives ker L=span{1}, so the columns are affinely independent. The maximum squared distance is strongly convex; its unique minimizer lies in the zero-sum plane and is fixed under permutations in the two classes. For c=(a1_p,−pa1_q/q), direct column inner products give D_A=q(q+1)+pNa²/q−2Na and D_B=p(p+1)+pNa²/q+2Npa/q. Their difference is (q−p)(N+1)−2N²a/q. The upper envelope follows D_A up to the crossing a_0, and follows D_B after it. On the latter interval D_B increases; D_A has its minimum at q/p. Thus a*=min(a_0,q/p). At the crossing the common squared distance is the average squared vertex norm plus ||c||², giving the first displayed radius; at q/p, D_A=q²(p−1)/p and D_A−D_B is the stated clearance. Contact weights (1+a)/N and (1−pa/q)/N are nonnegative at the optimum and map under L to c; in the screened case the latter vanish. This also directly certifies the global optimum. The screened-test integer numerator is −2 for (3,13) and 16 for (3,14), hence the cited clearance 16/3. Literal equality in the transition condition cannot occur for the allowed integers: it would force N+1 to divide 2N², thus to divide 2. Its stated contact behavior is a correct boundary description of the scalar minimization, not an actual integer instance.
residual_risks: The check script is finite; its SLSQP branch is restricted to N≤18 and starts near the predicted answer. The convex-contact identity, not that solver, guarantees global optimality. The metric is the full-column inherited Euclidean metric.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The vertex-transitive theorem does cover p=q: k=p and the centroid 0 is the optimal center by equal convex weights. It does not cover unequal degrees. A path-specific endpoint screening result is not a superfamily containing these bicliques.

evidence: Regular/more symmetric overlap only gives the balanced case. In unequal classes the circumsphere remains defined but need not minimize the enclosing radius. The different screening record uses −2p²+2q(q−2)p+q²(q−2) with additional generators.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The general contact-hull principle certifies a proposed solution but does not specify the active class or threshold for K_{p,q}. Finding whether the equidistant center lies before or beyond the smaller-class centroid, including strict clearance when the latter binds, requires the graph-specific distance calculation. Neither the width law, the symmetric radius nor the other screening polynomial implies it.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact Euclidean invariant of a standard family, with a complete classification of which vertices determine the minimal ball. The distinction between an equidistant circumsphere and an optimal ball has a concrete witness at adjacent parameters K_{3,13} and K_{3,14}; the formula also quantifies clearance throughout the latter phase. This is useful information beyond the balanced radius and beyond a numerical convex-hull test.
residual_risks: No inferred result for weighted or general bipartite Laplacians, or for a changed coordinate metric.
